terms.definition: The thin, flexible outer boundary that surrounds every cell and separates its insides from the outside.
terms.function: Controls what enters and leaves the cell.
terms.whyItMatters: It is what makes a cell a distinct, living unit in control of its internal conditions.

terms.definition: The double layer of phospholipid molecules that forms the main structure of the membrane.
terms.function: Provides a flexible barrier that small, simple molecules can slip through.
terms.whereItIs: The body of the membrane itself.
terms.whyItMatters: Its oily interior resists water crossing, which is the basis of selective movement.

terms.definition: The property of letting some substances through while blocking others.
terms.function: Allows the cell to pick and choose what crosses its border.
terms.whereItIs: In the membrane's structure and its protein doors.
terms.whyItMatters: It lets the cell keep its inside stable and safe from outside changes.

terms.definition: The ways molecules move across the cell membrane, from free movement to protein doors.
terms.function: Moves nutrients in, waste out, and helps the cell communicate.
terms.whereItIs: Occurs at the membrane surface and its proteins.
terms.whyItMatters: Feeding and cleaning the cell depends on transport across the membrane.
